description: Dedicated entries for cargo scales, packaging, and shipment security.

entries.title: One-Ton Cargo Load
entries.summary: Small shipments favor compact, valuable, urgent, medical, magical, or technical goods carried by fast vessels.
body: Typical loads include textiles, spices, rare metals, magical components, specialty rations, ammunition, medicine, artifacts, and repair tools. Reinforced crates, barrels, and pallets leave the carrier maneuverable and able to make quick port calls.

entries.title: Five-Ton Cargo Load
entries.summary: Standard merchant freight carries settlement supplies, weapons, water, machinery, trade goods, and moderate magical cargo.
body: Mid-sized ships use reinforced crates, barrels, and chests for preserved food, ammunition, rigging, engine components, water, spirits, textiles, ores, mana batteries, and potions. Careful distribution preserves flight balance.

entries.title: Ten-Ton Cargo Load
entries.summary: Bulk freight requires reinforced cargo ships and carries industrial materials, livestock, siege equipment, reserves, and powerful artifacts.
body: Heavy crates, chains, cargo bays, cages, and containment wards secure ore, lumber, metal, creatures, weaponry, armor, water, fuel, luxury goods, and magical objects. Strong lift and disciplined weight distribution are essential.

entries.title: Cargo Packaging and Security
entries.summary: Sky freight is wrapped, sealed, warded, weighed, marked, and tied down against weather, turbulence, theft, substitution, and sabotage.
body: Burlap, padded cloth, rope, treated twine, tarred canvas, oilcloth, iron-banded crates, airtight barrels, pallets, and cargo nets protect goods in flight.
Wax tablets, merchant insignia, signatures, weight checks, rune-sealed lids, illusory script, shocking wards, alert enchantments, and false-bottom crates expose or deter tampering.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: General Cargo Wrapping and Security Measures
